$comment: D-CSUBSET-VOID-TERNARY-LOWERS-A-PHI-OF-VOID: the runtime witness for C 6.5.15p3 — a conditional whose second and third operands are both `void` has void type, and is ordinary C that gcc 13.3.0 (-std=c2x) and clang 18.1.3 (-std=c23), probed SEPARATELY, compile and RUN. MEASURED at 301e2a63: all FIVE source shapes produced the SAME `error[L_UnsupportedLoweringForOpcode]: MIR value %N used ...`, an INTERNAL message two tiers below the source. One error text across five unrelated-looking syntaxes is what identified a single lowering step as the cause rather than five separate gaps: the ternary value path ends in a join Phi, Phi is a value-producing opcode whose result type must be valid, so a VOID result asked for a phi of something with no value. The fix lowers the diamond with NO join phi and discards each arm through the one discard funnel, which is also why all five shapes close together — the bare statement and the loop body are ExprStmts, the comma's left operand is a SeqExpr side-effect statement, and `(void)X` mints no Cast node at all (D-CSUBSET-CAST-VOID-DISCARD), so every one of them arrives at that funnel. exitCode 42 = every arm correct; any other exit IS the failing arm's id (1..11). EVERY ARM IS SIDE-EFFECTING AND COUNTED, never merely compiled: the failure a naive fix opens is running the WRONG arm, or BOTH, or NEITHER while still compiling, so `t` is volatile, each helper adds a distinct amount, and both branch directions are asserted separately — arm (1) alone would be satisfied by a diamond that always takes the `then` side, which is precisely what a broken one does. `sel` derives from argc so nothing folds, arm (7) nests one void conditional inside another's arm to prove the fix is not depth-1 only, and arms (8) re-assert the ordinary VALUE-producing ternary in both directions so the change cannot have disturbed the scalar diamond that still joins with a real phi. The release arm re-checks that the optimizer does not collapse a value-less diamond into nothing.
